Definition: from G3681; to defame, i.e. rail at, chide, taunt:--cast in teeth, (suffer) reproach, revile, upbraid.
BiblicalUsage: Oneidizo means to revile, to reproach, to cast in the teeth. Jesus blesses those who are reviled for His sake in Matthew 5:11 and Luke 6:22, and the same word is thrown at Him on the cross in Mark 15:32, where those crucified with Him revile Him. Romans 15:3 says the reproaches of those who reproached God fell on Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the reviling of Jesus is the proof He took our place, because the taunts meant for God fell on Him. That is why I hold that being reviled for His sake is a blessing, not a shame, the cross has already carried the worst of it.
